# MCP Nim SDK

A Nim implementation of the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP): a client, a server, and the stdio and Streamable HTTP transports.

This checkout speaks MCP **2026-07-28** and every earlier version: `2024-11-05`, `2025-03-26`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-11-25`, `2026-07-28`. A client and a server settle on the newest version both speak; see [docs/versions.md](docs/versions.md).

## Features of 2026-07-28

52 of the 52 features of `2026-07-28` are implemented in this tree. The table lists every feature the specification of `2026-07-28` defines; "not implemented" means this SDK does not do it yet.

## Install

Nim 2.2.12 or newer. In your `.nimble` file:

```nim
requires "https://github.com/jasagiri/mcp-nim-sdk#mcp-2026-07-28"
```

Then `import mcp`. A program file of your own cannot be called `mcp.nim`: the import would find that file instead of the SDK.

## A server

Serves one tool, `echo`, on stdin and stdout ([examples/stdio_server.nim](examples/stdio_server.nim)):

```nim
## An MCP server on stdin/stdout with one tool, `echo`.
##
##   nim c -r examples/stdio_server.nim
##
## Speaks the build's default protocol version and every earlier one. Stdout
## carries the protocol, so anything for people goes to stderr.

import std/[asyncdispatch, json, options]
import mcp

proc main() =
  let server = newMcpServer(
    McpServerInfo(name: "echo-server", version: "0.1.0"),
    capabilities = McpServerCapabilities(tools: some(McpToolsCapability())))

  let listTools: typeof(McpToolHandlers().listHandler.get) =
    proc(): Future[seq[JsonNode]] {.async.} =
      return @[%*{
        "name": "echo",
        "description": "Returns the text it is given",
        "inputSchema": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {"text": {"type": "string"}},
          "required": ["text"]}}]

  let callTool: typeof(McpToolHandlers().callHandler.get) =
    proc(name: string, arguments: JsonNode): Future[JsonNode] {.async.} =
      if name != "echo":
        raise newException(ValueError, "Unknown tool: " & name)
      return %*{"content": [{"type": "text", "text": arguments{"text"}.getStr()}],
                "isError": false}

  server.setToolHandlers(McpToolHandlers(
    listHandler: some(listTools), callHandler: some(callTool)))

  server.transport = newStdioTransport()
  waitFor server.processMessages()

main()
```

## A client

Starts that server as a child process, lists its tools and calls `echo` ([examples/stdio_client.nim](examples/stdio_client.nim)):

```nim
## An MCP client that starts a server as a child process, lists its tools and
## calls `echo`.
##
##   nim c examples/stdio_server.nim
##   nim c -r examples/stdio_client.nim examples/stdio_server

import std/[asyncdispatch, json, options, os]
import mcp

proc run(command: string, args: seq[string]) {.async.} =
  let client = newMcpClient(McpClientInfo(name: "echo-client", version: "0.1.0"))
  await client.connect(newProcessTransport(command, args))
  echo "connected, protocol version ", client.negotiatedVersion.get

  let listed = await client.sendRequest("tools/list", newJObject())
  if listed.error.isSome:
    raise newException(ValueError, "tools/list failed: " & listed.error.get.message)
  for tool in listed.result.get{"tools"}:
    echo "tool: ", tool{"name"}.getStr()

  let called = await client.sendRequest("tools/call",
    %*{"name": "echo", "arguments": {"text": "hello"}})
  if called.error.isSome:
    raise newException(ValueError, "tools/call failed: " & called.error.get.message)
  echo "echo says: ", called.result.get{"content"}{0}{"text"}.getStr()

  await client.close()

if paramCount() < 1:
  stderr.writeLine "usage: stdio_client SERVER_COMMAND [ARGS...]"
  quit(2)
waitFor run(paramStr(1), commandLineParams()[1 .. ^1])
```

```sh
nim c examples/stdio_server.nim
nim c -r examples/stdio_client.nim examples/stdio_server
```

The same pair over Streamable HTTP is in [examples/http_server.nim](examples/http_server.nim) and [examples/http_client.nim](examples/http_client.nim).

## Turning features on

There are two switches. **Which protocol versions** a program speaks is decided when it is compiled. **Which features** it offers is decided in its code: a feature is on when the program declares it and registers what answers it. Nothing is on by default except the protocol itself.

### 1. Protocol versions, at compile time

A build speaks a range of versions, from its oldest to its default. This checkout's default is `2026-07-28`.

| Define | Meaning | Default here |
|---|---|---|
| `-d:mcpDefaultProtocolVersion=<version>` | the newest version the build speaks | `2026-07-28` |
| `-d:mcpOldestProtocolVersion=<version>` | the oldest version the build speaks | `2024-11-05` |
| `-d:ssl` | `https://` URLs in the HTTP client and in authorization | off |

```sh
# Everything up to 2026-07-28 (what this checkout does without any define)
nim c yourprogram.nim

# Speak nothing newer than 2025-06-18
nim c -d:mcpDefaultProtocolVersion=2025-06-18 yourprogram.nim

# Speak 2026-07-28 alone: no initialize handshake, no sessions, no HTTP+SSE
nim c -d:mcpOldestProtocolVersion=2026-07-28 yourprogram.nim

# Connect to https:// servers
nim c -d:ssl yourprogram.nim
```

To make a define permanent, put it in your project's `config.nims`:

```nim
switch("define", "mcpDefaultProtocolVersion=2025-06-18")
switch("define", "ssl")
```

or in its `nim.cfg`:

```
-d:mcpDefaultProtocolVersion=2025-06-18
-d:ssl
```

A version that is not a released one, or an oldest version newer than the default, stops the compilation with a message that names the define. A server or client created for a version outside the range raises `ValueError`.

Within the range, one server can be held to an older ceiling at run time, for example to serve only up to `2025-03-26`:

```nim
let server = newMcpServer(info, protocolVersion = mpv20250326, capabilities = caps)
```

When this SDK is a dependency, name the branch of the version you want in your `.nimble` file (see [Install](#install)); the branch sets the default, and the defines above still apply. When working in a checkout of this repository, `nim.cfg` already adds `src` to the path; elsewhere pass `--path:<checkout>/src`.

Requirements: Nim 2.2.12 or newer, the default memory management (`--mm:orc`), and the `uuids` and `nimcrypto` packages (nimcrypto computes SHA-256 and HMAC-SHA256, which the standard library does not have, for PKCE, the sealed request state and the signed webhooks). No other define is needed; there is none per feature.

Three packages from the same foundation tree are not in the nimble registry and are found by path: `nim-bearer-challenge` (reads `WWW-Authenticate` challenges, for the OAuth client and the resource server), `nim-secret` (compares secrets in constant time, for the HMAC checks) and `nim-loopback` (decides whether a Host, an Origin or a bind address is loopback, for the HTTP server's checks). Check them out next to this repository (`../nim-bearer-challenge`, `../nim-secret`, `../nim-loopback`), where `nim.cfg` finds them; elsewhere pass `--path:` to each one's `src`.

### 2. Features, at run time

A server declares a capability in `newMcpServer` and registers the handlers that answer it. A client registers a handler before `connect`, which declares the capability for it. Each side is then offered only what the version the two settled on has, so the same program serves old and new peers.

[examples/features_server.nim](examples/features_server.nim) turns on everything a server has in the core protocol:

```nim
## A server that turns on every server-side feature of the core protocol:
## tools, resources (with subscriptions), prompts, completion and logging.
##
##   nim c -r examples/features_server.nim
##
## A feature is on when its capability is declared in `newMcpServer` and its
## handlers are registered; nothing else is needed. The server offers a
## client only what the version they settled on has.

import std/[asyncdispatch, json, options]
import mcp

proc main() =
  let server = newMcpServer(
    McpServerInfo(name: "features-server", version: "0.1.0"),
    capabilities = McpServerCapabilities(
      tools: some(McpToolsCapability(listChanged: true)),
      resources: some(McpResourcesCapability(subscribe: true, listChanged: true)),
      prompts: some(McpPromptsCapability(listChanged: true)),
      completions: some(McpCompletionsCapability()),
      logging: some(McpLoggingCapability())))

  # Tools. The arguments of a call are checked against `inputSchema` before
  # the handler runs.
  server.onToolsList(proc(cursor: Option[string]): Future[McpPage] {.async.} =
    return McpPage(items: @[%*{
      "name": "add",
      "description": "Adds two integers",
      "inputSchema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"a": {"type": "integer"}, "b": {"type": "integer"}},
        "required": ["a", "b"]}}]))
  server.onToolCall(proc(ctx: McpRequestContext, name: string,
                         arguments: JsonNode): Future[JsonNode] {.async.} =
    if name != "add":
      raise newUnknownTool(name)
    # Progress reaches the client only when its request asked for it;
    # log messages only at the level the client asked for.
    await ctx.reportProgress(0.5)
    await ctx.log(mllInfo, %"adding")
    let sum = arguments["a"].getInt() + arguments["b"].getInt()
    return %*{"content": [{"type": "text", "text": $sum}]})

  # Resources.
  server.onResourcesList(proc(cursor: Option[string]): Future[McpPage] {.async.} =
    return McpPage(items: @[%*{"uri": "memo://greeting", "name": "greeting",
                               "mimeType": "text/plain"}]))
  server.onResourceRead(proc(ctx: McpRequestContext,
                             uri: string): Future[seq[JsonNode]] {.async.} =
    if uri != "memo://greeting":
      raise newResourceNotFound(uri)
    return @[%*{"uri": uri, "mimeType": "text/plain", "text": "hello"}])

  # Prompts.
  server.onPromptsList(proc(cursor: Option[string]): Future[McpPage] {.async.} =
    return McpPage(items: @[%*{
      "name": "greet", "description": "Greets someone",
      "arguments": [{"name": "who", "required": true}]}]))
  server.onPromptGet(proc(ctx: McpRequestContext, name: string,
                          arguments: JsonNode): Future[JsonNode] {.async.} =
    if name != "greet":
      raise newInvalidParams("Unknown prompt: " & name)
    return %*{"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": {
      "type": "text", "text": "Say hello to " & arguments{"who"}.getStr()}}]})

  # Completion of prompt arguments and resource template variables.
  server.onComplete(proc(ctx: McpRequestContext,
                         request: McpCompletionRequest): Future[McpCompletion] {.async.} =
    var names: seq[string]
    for name in ["Ada", "Alan", "Grace"]:
      if request.argumentValue.len == 0 or name[0] == request.argumentValue[0]:
        names.add name
    return McpCompletion(values: names))

  server.transport = newStdioTransport()
  waitFor server.processMessages()

main()
```

The example writes its tool definition and its result as JSON. A server can build them with procedures instead: `createToolInfo` with `createInputSchema` and the `create…Property` procedures for an item of `tools/list`, and `createToolResult` with `createTextToolContent` and the other `create…ToolContent` procedures for the answer of a call ([src/server/tools.nim](src/server/tools.nim)). They produce the same JSON and leave out the fields that were not given.

A tool's `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` are validated as JSON Schema 2020-12, which a schema without `$schema` is taken to be, or as draft-07 when the schema names it. A schema that names any other dialect is refused with `UnsupportedDialectError`: a schema the SDK cannot check is reported, never taken as satisfied.

[examples/features_client.nim](examples/features_client.nim) does the same for a client:

```nim
## A client that turns on every client-side feature of the core protocol:
## roots, sampling and elicitation.
##
##   nim c examples/features_server.nim
##   nim c -r examples/features_client.nim examples/features_server
##
## A feature is on when its handler is registered before `connect`; the
## registration declares the capability. The client offers a server only
## what the version they settled on has.

import std/[asyncdispatch, json, options, os]
import mcp

proc run(command: string, args: seq[string]) {.async.} =
  let client = newMcpClient(McpClientInfo(name: "features-client", version: "0.1.0"))

  # Roots: the directories the server may work in.
  client.setRootsProvider(proc(): Future[seq[McpRoot]] {.async.} =
    return @[McpRoot(uri: "file://" & getCurrentDir(), name: some("work"))])

  # Sampling: the server asks this client's model for a completion. A real
  # host shows the request to its user before it runs a model.
  client.setSamplingHandler(proc(request: McpSamplingRequest): Future[McpSamplingResult] {.async.} =
    return McpSamplingResult(role: "assistant", model: "none",
      content: McpContentItem(kind: mckText, text: "(no model attached)"),
      stopReason: some("endTurn")))

  # Elicitation: the server asks the user for input. Declining is always
  # an answer.
  client.setElicitationHandler(proc(request: McpElicitRequest): Future[McpElicitResult] {.async.} =
    return McpElicitResult(action: eaDecline))

  await client.connect(newProcessTransport(command, args))
  echo "connected, protocol version ", client.negotiatedVersion.get

  for tool in (await client.listTools()).tools:
    echo "tool: ", tool.name
  let sum = await client.callTool("add", %*{"a": 2, "b": 3})
  echo "2 + 3 = ", sum.contentItems[0].text

  await client.close()

if paramCount() < 1:
  stderr.writeLine "usage: features_client SERVER_COMMAND [ARGS...]"
  quit(2)
waitFor run(paramStr(1), commandLineParams()[1 .. ^1])
```

```sh
nim c examples/features_server.nim
nim c -r examples/features_client.nim examples/features_server
```

#### Server features

| Feature | Declare in `McpServerCapabilities` | Register or call |
|---|---|---|
| Tools | `tools: some(McpToolsCapability(listChanged: ...))` | `onToolsList`, `onToolCall`; `notifyToolListChanged` |
| Tool input validation | nothing: always on | the `inputSchema` of each tool in the list |
| Structured tool output | nothing: a result is always checked | `outputSchema` in the tool, `structuredContent` in the result |
| Resources | `resources: some(McpResourcesCapability(subscribe: ..., listChanged: ...))` | `onResourcesList`, `onResourceTemplatesList`, `onResourceRead`; `notifyResourceListChanged` |
| Resource subscriptions | `subscribe: true` in the resources capability | `notifyResourceUpdated(uri)`; optionally `onResourceSubscribe`, `onResourceUnsubscribe` |
| Prompts | `prompts: some(McpPromptsCapability(listChanged: ...))` | `onPromptsList`, `onPromptGet`; `notifyPromptListChanged` |
| Completion | `completions: some(McpCompletionsCapability())` | `onComplete` |
| Logging | `logging: some(McpLoggingCapability())` | `ctx.log(level, data)` in a handler, `server.log(...)` outside one |
| Pagination | nothing | return `nextCursor` in `McpPage`, or wrap a whole list with `pagedList(all, pageSize)` |
| Progress | nothing | `ctx.reportProgress(...)`; sent only when the request asked for progress |
| Cancellation | nothing | read `ctx.cancelled` in a long handler |
| Asking the client (before 2026-07-28) | nothing; the client must have declared the capability | `ctx.createMessage` (sampling), `ctx.listRoots`, `ctx.ping` |
| Asking the user (before 2026-07-28) | nothing; the client must have declared `elicitation` | `ctx.elicit(message, requestedSchema)` |
| Sending the user to a page (2025-11-25) | nothing; the client must have declared `elicitation.url` | `ctx.elicitUrl(message, elicitationId, url)` |
| Asking the client (2026-07-28: multi round-trip) | nothing; the client must have declared the capability | `ctx.requireInput(key, method, params)` in a tool, prompt or resource handler |
| Tasks (2025-11-25 only) | `server.enableTasks()` declares it | `execution.taskSupport` in the tool; `enableTasks` returns the store |
| `subscriptions/listen` (2026-07-28) | the `listChanged` and `subscribe` flags above | the same `notify...` calls; `endSubscriptions` to close them |
| Parameter headers (2026-07-28, HTTP) | nothing | `"x-mcp-header": "Name"` on a property of a tool's `inputSchema` |
| Extensions (2026-07-28) | `server.registerExtension(id, settings)` declares it | `registerExtensionMethod` for the methods the extension defines |

#### Client features

| Feature | Register before `connect` | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Roots | `client.setRootsProvider(provider)` | declares `roots` |
| Sampling | `client.setSamplingHandler(handler)` | declares `sampling` |
| Tool use in sampling (2025-11-25) | `client.setSamplingHandler(handler, tools = true)` | declares `sampling.tools` as well |
| Elicitation | `client.setElicitationHandler(handler)` | declares `elicitation` (form mode) |
| URL elicitation (2025-11-25) | `client.setElicitationHandler(handler, modes = {emForm, emUrl})` | declares `elicitation.url` as well |
| Tasks (2025-11-25 only) | `client.enableClientTasks(config)` | after the handlers of the requests to run as tasks are set; `callToolAsTask` and `waitForTask` to use a server's tasks |
| Multi round-trip requests (2026-07-28) | the handlers above | the client answers a server's input requests from them and retries, up to `maxInputRounds` |
| `subscriptions/listen` (2026-07-28) | nothing | `client.listen(...)` returns a subscription; `cancel` ends it |
| Extensions (2026-07-28) | `client.declareExtension(id, settings)` | `serverExtension(id)` tells whether the server has it; `callExtension` calls its methods |
| Timeouts, cancellation, progress | nothing | per request, in `McpRequestOptions`: `timeoutMs`, `cancel`, `onProgress` |
| Trace context (2026-07-28) | nothing | `traceContext` in `McpRequestOptions`; a server handler reads `ctx.traceContext` |

Using a server's tools, resources and prompts needs no registration: `listTools`, `callTool`, `listResources`, `readResource`, `listPrompts`, `getPrompt` and `complete` raise `McpUnsupportedError` when the server did not declare the capability.

#### Transports

| Transport | Server | Client |
|---|---|---|
| stdio | `server.transport = newStdioTransport()` then `processMessages()` | `newProcessTransport(command, args)` starts the server as a child process |
| Streamable HTTP | `newHttpServerTransport(host, port, path)`, `listen()`, `server.attachTransport(...)` | `newStreamableHttpTransport(url)` |
| HTTP+SSE (2024-11-05, deprecated) | `newHttpServerTransport(host, port, path)` serves it on `legacySsePath` (`/sse`); set that to `""` to turn it off | `newSseLegacyTransport(url)` |
| Either HTTP transport | the same server transport serves both | `newAutoHttpTransport(url)` tries Streamable HTTP first and falls back to HTTP+SSE |

The HTTP server accepts requests from loopback origins only; add others to `transport.allowedOrigins`. See [docs/transports.md](docs/transports.md).

#### Authorization

Authorization is off until it is attached to an HTTP transport. A server sets `transport.auth = newResourceServerAuth(config)` with a token verifier of its own, and every MCP endpoint the transport serves then needs a token; a client sets `transport.auth` to an OAuth client made with `newOAuthClient`; a client secret is configured together with the issuer of the authorization server it belongs to, and is sent to no other. Both live in `auth/` and are imported separately (`import auth/resource_server`, `import auth/client`). Build with `-d:ssl`: authorization servers are reached over `https://`. When a server keeps answering 401 or 403 and nothing more can be done about it, the request fails with `McpAuthorizationError`, a `McpTransportError` that carries the HTTP `status`; `connect` fails with it too, without trying the handshake of another protocol version.

### 3. Extensions

Extensions are optional additions to MCP that the two sides agree on by name. Each is a module of its own under `src/ext/`, and none of them is part of `import mcp`. An extension is on only in a program that imports its module **and** calls what turns it on; there is no define for any of them, and a module that is not imported is not compiled in.

This checkout carries the mechanism (`registerExtension`, `registerExtensionMethod`, `declareExtension`, in the tables above) and no extension of its own. The official extensions are on the branch `mcp-2026-07-28-ext`, and the draft ones on `mcp-draft`.

### Checking a build

```sh
nimble test                # every test with this checkout's default version
nimble testAllVersions     # the same, once per released version as the default
nim c -r -d:mcpDefaultProtocolVersion=2025-06-18 tests/external/test_legacy_handshake.nim
```

The property tests (`tests/external/test_*_prop.nim`) use nim-propcheck, a package that is not published: `nim.cfg` reads it from `../nim-propcheck/src`, so the tests need it checked out beside this directory. A program that uses the SDK does not need it.

On a branch that adds to another, `MCP_TEST_BASE=<commit> nimble testAllVersions` runs this checkout's default version in full and, for the other versions, only the tests built from a file that differs from that commit; `MCP_TEST_BASE=<commit> nimble affectedTests` lists them. It reads what the compiler recorded when it last built each test, so a file that only an older version compiles in is not seen: run without `MCP_TEST_BASE` before a release.

`DefaultProtocolVersion`, `OldestProtocolVersion` and `SupportedProtocolVersions` (in `protocol/version`, exported by `mcp`) tell a program what it was built to speak.

## Running a server on a network

A server on the HTTP transport refuses, by default, what one caller could use against the others. The limits are fields of the transport; set them after `newHttpServerTransport`.

| What | Default | Field |
|---|---|---|
| The `Host` header names this server | bound to loopback: loopback names only; bound elsewhere: not checked until names are listed | `allowedHosts` |
| The `Origin` header, when a browser sends one | loopback origins only | `allowedOrigins` |
| Size of a request body | 4 MiB | `maxBodySize` (argument of `newHttpServerTransport`) |
| Sessions, in all and per client address | limited; a full transport gives up a session that was never used before it refuses | `maxSessions`, `maxSessionsPerPeer` |
| Requests in progress and messages waiting | limited; more are refused with 503 and `Retry-After` | `maxPendingRequests`, `maxQueuedMessages` |

Behind a reverse proxy that passes the public name on, list that name: `transport.allowedHosts = @["mcp.example.com"]`. A header such as `X-Forwarded-For` is not trusted; the client address is the peer of the TCP connection, which behind a proxy is the proxy.

A client has 30 seconds to send a whole request (`newHttpServerTransport(readTimeoutMs = ...)`; 0 turns the limit off). One that sends nothing, or stops halfway, loses the connection: with a `408` if its request line had arrived, without an answer otherwise. On a keep-alive connection the time also bounds the wait between requests; the time a handler takes, an event stream included, is not limited. The limit is `readTimeout` of Nim's `asynchttpserver` ([nim-lang/Nim#26352](https://github.com/nim-lang/Nim/pull/26352), Nim 2.3.1); with an older Nim the SDK uses a copy of that module (`src/transport/vendor/asynchttpserver.nim`, under Nim's MIT license).

A client is guarded the other way round: what it fetches because a server said so (authorization metadata, icons) is refused when the address is loopback, link-local or reserved, and when it is private unless `allowPrivateNetworks` is set; a response is limited in size (`maxResponseSize`) and a connection in time (`connectTimeoutMs`).

Over https the certificate has to be valid for the host the URL names. A client whose servers use a private certificate authority names its certificates in `caFile` (on the HTTP client transports, in `IconFetchOptions` and in the authorization `FetchPolicy`), which replaces the system's authorities for those requests.

## Changes that break code written for earlier commits

These came with the security review of 2026-10-06 and with the reading of the specification sentence by sentence of 2026-10-13. Each refuses something that used to be accepted.

| Was | Is now |
|---|---|
| A transport bound to a loopback address answered any `Host` | It answers loopback names and those in `allowedHosts`; others get 403 |
| A JSON Schema of any depth and a `pattern` of any cost were checked | Checking stops with `SchemaLimitError` or `RegexLimitError` beyond the limits (`SchemaLimits`, `RegexLimits`); patterns are matched without backtracking, so a hostile one costs time in proportion to the text |
| A string that is not UTF-8 in a message was written as it was | A request or a notification that holds one is not sent (`McpTransportError`); a response is sent as an internal error. Nothing is replaced |
| A handler's result the specification does not allow was passed on | The peer gets an internal error and the cause goes to stderr: an image or a `blob` that is not base64, an image without `mimeType`, an embedded resource without `uri`, `mimeType` and `text` or `blob`, and, where the version has them, an `inputSchema` that is not an object schema (2025-11-25 on; its root `type: "object"` in 2026-07-28), a `ttlMs` below zero or a `cacheScope` other than `public` and `private` (2026-07-28) |
| `prompts/get` called the handler whatever the arguments | A required argument of the listed prompt that is missing, or `arguments` that is not an object, is answered with invalid params and the handler is not called |
| The request id a caller chose could repeat | `ValueError` for an id in flight; before 2026-07-28 also for an id the session has used (the client remembers up to `MaxChosenRequestIds` of them and refuses a further one) |
| A client answered a root that is no `file://` URI as it was | The server gets an internal error and the cause goes to stderr |
| A client's handler that raised sent the exception's whole text, with the traceback of a debug build | It sends the message alone |
| A request whose event stream ended before the response was answered by the transport with an error of its own making (`ErrStreamClosed`) | No message stands in for the response. The transport calls `onRequestLost`; the client raises `McpRequestLostError` (a `McpTransportError`), never `McpRequestError`. `ErrStreamClosed` is gone |
| A client sent whatever the caller asked while `initialize` was unanswered | Until the answer it sends `initialize` and `ping` only; anything else raises `McpError` and is not written |
| A client never pinged on its own | Before 2026-07-28 it pings a connection that has been idle for `pingIntervalMs` (30000; 0 turns it off). A ping unanswered for `pingTimeoutMs` closes the client and the waiting requests end with `McpConnectionClosedError` |
| A server served every request it was sent | One sender gets `maxRequestsPerSecond` (100; 0 turns it off). A request over it is answered with the error 429 (`ErrRateLimited`, with `data.retryAfterMs`) and no handler runs. The sender is the principal of the authorization, else the session, else the address of the TCP peer, else the connection. Behind a reverse proxy every client has the proxy's address: set the limit for all of them together, or turn it off and limit at the proxy. No forwarded header is trusted |
| A server sent every progress notification a handler reported | For one request it sends `maxProgressPerSecond` (20; 0 turns it off). What is held back is dropped, except the latest, which is sent before the response |
| A request answered with HTTP 404 in a session raised an HTTP error and the client kept the ended session | The client starts a new session with one `initialize` and raises `McpSessionExpiredError` (`renewed` says whether that worked). It does not send the request again: the caller decides |
| A server closed the first connection of a stream a second one took over without a word | It sends the SSE `retry` field first (`sseRetryMs`, 1000; 0 sends none) and says on stderr that the stream was taken over |
| `createMessage` sent `includeContext` of `thisServer` or `allServers` to any client (2025-11-25 on), and a `tool_result` whatever its `structuredContent` | `McpCapabilityError` unless the client declared `sampling.context`; `McpPayloadError` when the `structuredContent` does not conform to the `outputSchema` of its tool |
| `requireInputs` and `newInputRequired` let a later request replace an earlier one under the same key | `McpPayloadError` |
| A 2026-07-28 client answered a request of the server with method not found | It writes no response, as the specification asks, and says so on stderr |
| `newResourceServerAuth(config, mcpPath)` protected one path | `newResourceServerAuth(config)`: the transport protects every MCP endpoint it serves |
| A pre-registered client's secret went to whichever authorization server the MCP server named | `PreRegisteredClient` with a `clientSecret` needs `issuer`; the secret is sent to that authorization server only |
| `newTaskStore()` kept any number of tasks for any time | A `ttl` above 24 hours is lowered to it; one owner has 16 active and 256 kept tasks, the store 4096. Pass `maxTtlMs = none(int64)` and 0 for a count to lift a limit |

## Other versions

Each protocol version has a branch and a tag named `mcp-<version>`. Check one out, or name it in your `.nimble` file as above, and the SDK speaks that version and the earlier ones; its README, docs and examples describe exactly that version.

| Version | Branch | Handshake | This build |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2024-11-05` | `mcp-2024-11-05` | `initialize` | speaks |
| `2025-03-26` | `mcp-2025-03-26` | `initialize` | speaks |
| `2025-06-18` | `mcp-2025-06-18` | `initialize` | speaks |
| `2025-11-25` | `mcp-2025-11-25` | `initialize` | speaks |
| `2026-07-28` | `mcp-2026-07-28` | none, every request carries its metadata | speaks |
